_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The Lord is a stronghold for the oppressed, a refuge in trouble.
Those who know your name put their trust in you.
The wind howled and the waves broke into the boat.
And Jesus rose and said: Peace. Be still.
We come with sword and spear too small for our giants.
We come in the name of the Lord of hosts.
Come, let us worship the God who calms the sea.
We come, and we are not afraid. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Night on the water, the waves breaking over the side, the boat already filling, and you wonder if the One asleep in the stern even cares.
Peace. Be still.
Whatever giant stands over you, taller and louder than your faith, remember the boy who ran at it with five smooth stones and the name of God.
Peace. Be still.
The Lord is a refuge for the crushed, a stronghold in the time of trouble; the storm has never once had the last word.
Peace. Be still.
So come into the boat, all of you who are afraid; the wind drops, the sea goes glassy, and a great calm settles over the water.
Peace. Be still, and know that God is here.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The waves break in; the boat is filling.
Peace. Be still.
You are a refuge when the giants roar.
Peace. Be still.
Jesus stands; the wind lies down.
Peace. Be still.
Come, let us worship; do not be afraid.
Peace. Be still. Amen.
